title: Boy George Pulls Out of Jesus Christ Superstar Over Pro-Israel Song Controversy
excerpt: The Culture Club frontman’s manager withdrew him from the West End production at the London Palladium days before his August 3 debut as King Herod.
body:
• Boy George has withdrawn from the West End production of Jesus Christ Superstar at the London Palladium, days before his scheduled August 3 debut as King Herod
  • The withdrawal follows controversy over his new track "We Will Dance Again," which voices support for Israel's military action in Palestine
  • His manager Paul Kemsley said the decision was made "with the utmost respect for the producers" and in the "best interests" of the artist
  • Boy George was one of six stars sharing the King Herod role in the limited summer run starring Sam Ryder as Jesus

Boy George will no longer appear in the West End production of Jesus Christ Superstar at the London Palladium, his management confirmed Thursday, pulling the Culture Club frontman from the show just days before he was due to take the stage as King Herod.

The 65-year-old Grammy Award-winning singer had been scheduled to perform from August 3 to 15 as part of a star-studded limited summer run of the Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber musical, which features Sam Ryder in the title role of Jesus.

The Song That Sparked the Row

The withdrawal follows backlash over Boy George's new track "We Will Dance Again," which voices support for Israel's military action in Palestine. The song placed the singer at the center of the ongoing cultural debate over the Gaza conflict and drew criticism from pro-Palestinian campaigners.

Boy George had previously voiced support for Israeli singer Noam Bettan, who faced boycott threats ahead of a performance, saying the artist should be allowed to perform regardless of the political context.

Manager's Statement

The decision to withdraw was made by Boy George's manager, Paul Kemsley, who posted a statement on Facebook.

"George has never been afraid to stand by his personal convictions, and I have always respected him for that. Equally, I believe it is my responsibility to make decisions that are in the best interests of my artist while also showing respect to others."

— Paul Kemsley, Boy George's Manager

Kemsley apologized to fans who had purchased tickets specifically to see Boy George perform, acknowledging the "disappointment" while emphasizing that the decision was made "with the utmost respect for the producers, the creative team and the entire company."

A Star-Studded Herod Lineup

The Jesus Christ Superstar production had cast six different performers to share the role of King Herod across its June 20 to September 5 run. Jesse Tyler Ferguson (Modern Family) played the part from June 20 to July 11, followed by Sir Simon Russell Beale (July 13-25), Richard Armitage (July 27 to August 1), and now Boy George's vacated slot of August 3-15. Layton Williams takes over August 17-29, with Julian Clary closing out the run.

It remains unclear whether the production will announce a replacement for Boy George's dates or redistribute the performances among the remaining cast.

The controversy reflects the increasingly polarized cultural landscape around the Israel-Palestine conflict, where artists face growing pressure from both sides. For London's diverse diaspora communities, including the significant Indian and South Asian populations who frequent the West End, the episode underscores how geopolitical tensions are reshaping the entertainment industry.
